messages:
Priya Rao: Hey team — customer (Acme Finance) reports streaming responses cut off mid-chunk after ~45–120s. Client reconnects repeatedly and they see duplicate billing and partial outputs. Attaching client log excerpt and a curl trace.

Ken Liu: Thanks Priya. Do we have any server-side errors? Any 5xx or auth 401? Also which proxy in front (nginx/traefik/cloud)?

Priya Rao: They use our hosted API in us-east, routed through our edge nginx pool. No 5xx in request logs; upstream shows 200 then abrupt close. Example from client: 

```
[fetch] received partial: "data: {\"id\": \"msg_123\", \"text\": \"Hello wo"
socket error: write EPIPE
reconnect attempt 1
reconnect attempt 2
```

Devon Matthews: EPIPE on client means server closed socket while kernel still had data queued. On our side I've seen send(2) return EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK then higher layer decides to abort after X retries. Can you paste the server send error traces?

Priya Rao: Pasted from prod host /var/log/redwood/edge-1.log: 

```
2026-03-15T18:14:02Z stream: writev failed: errno=11 EAGAIN
2026-03-15T18:14:02Z stream: send retry=1
2026-03-15T18:14:02Z stream: send retry=2
2026-03-15T18:14:02Z stream: send failed, aborting connection, conn_id=cn-45f2
```

Devon Matthews: Ok this looks like backpressure from the client side (slow consumer). Our runtime currently has a conservative send retry loop then aborts to avoid head-of-line congestion. Two things to confirm: (1) is there an upstream proxy buffering (nginx proxy_buffering on) causing bursts? (2) is client reading super slowly (e.g., sleeping between reads)?

Priya Rao: Customer dev says they intentionally slow-parse to reduce CPU: they read ~1KB every 700ms. They also show nginx with default buffering.

Ken Liu: That matches. Nginx proxy_buffering combined with slow reader can cause kernel sndbuf to fill; send becomes EAGAIN. When our code hits retry threshold we close. That results in truncated chunks and client reconnects (duplicate work + billing).

Marta (billing): They opened a billing dispute — spike corresponds to ~1.6x requests during the reconnect storms. We can do goodwill credits, but engineering recommendation first.

Devon Matthews: Repro script we use locally (Node) to mimic slow consumer: 

```js
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
(async () => {
  const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=...',{headers:{Authorization:'Bearer x'}});
  const reader = res.body.getReader();
  while(true){
    const {done,value} = await reader.read();
    if(done) break;
    // slow parse 
    await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,700));
    console.log('got chunk', value && value.length);
  }
})();
```

Devon Matthews: Repro steps: run above and watch server-side send retries; try toggling nginx proxy_buffering off (proxy_set_header X-Accel-Buffering off) and see difference. Also repro by setting SO_SNDBUF small on server to force EAGAIN quickly.

Priya Rao: Customer tried disabling nginx buffering with no change (they said they still saw truncated stream). They confirmed client code sleeps 700ms.

Ken Liu: If buffering off didn't help, possibly the proxy still has kernel-level socket buffers or there is an intermediate CDN we don't control. Can you confirm route with traceroute and verify there is no intermediate buffering?

Priya Rao: Traceroute shows no extra hop besides our edge and their corporate proxy. Their corp proxy is squid, might buffer. They tested bypassing it from a dev VM and the issue disappears.

Devon Matthews: Good find — corporate proxy is the slow consumer middlebox. That explains why disabling buffering on our nginx didn't help. Two mitigations: 
- Server side: increase send retry window and enlarge kernel sndbuf via sysctl for dedicated hosts serving them (temporary).
- Client side: suggest they use backpressure-aware reader (read smaller chunks or avoid 700ms sleeps) or use a polling/fanout pattern instead of long-lived SSE.
- Platform: rate-limit repeated reconnects for the same session id so we don't bill duplicates immediately; add dedupe-id header and idempotent handling at billing pipeline.

Ken Liu: Also short term we can lower abort aggressiveness: bump retry count from 2->6 and increase exponential backoff between retries. But this increases memory pressure and could affect other tenants — needs SRE signoff.

Priya Rao: Customer accepts client changes but asks for platform tweaks to avoid billing impact while they roll fixes (will take 2 weeks).

Marta (billing): We can apply a temporary credit for spike and set billing hold while engineering investigates. Please create a support ticket with the credit amount request and expected window.

Devon Matthews: Action items: 
1) I'll run a canary config on a small edge pool to bump send retry and sndbuf for the next 24h to see if reconnect storms subside.
2) Priya please collect full traceroute + their corp proxy config (squid) and a minimal repro that bypasses corp proxy.
3) Ken/SRE please review memory / fds impact of longer retry loops.

Priya Rao: Will collect repro and ping when I have corp proxy config. Thanks. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deployment started: edge-canary/stream-retry-bump -> 3 hosts

Devon Matthews: Canary live. Early telemetry shows per-conn aborts dropped from ~12/min to ~1. Still seeing duplicate reconnects but much reduced.

Marta (billing): Confirmed billing hold and pending credit for Acme Finance. I'll DM details.

Ken Liu: Follow-ups: add a diagnostic header X-Redwood-SSE-Session-ID to outgoing SSE responses so support can correlate reconnect storms to a single session id for future disputes. Also add a soft rate-limit that returns 429 if same session reconnects too fast (while preserving user data for idempotent clients).

Priya Rao: Got it. Closing loop once customer validates.

Devon Matthews: Notes for runbook: when customers report partial chunks + write EAGAIN/EPIPE: check for intermediate buffering (corporate proxies), reproduce with slow-reader scripts, consider temporary sndbuf bump and retry-window increase, add reconnect rate-limiting and session dedupe in billing pipeline.

Priya Rao: Thanks everyone.
